findings.evidence: Frame 1 shows the left wire framing its cell. From 25% on, only a tiny orange stub shows at the cell's foot. The code caps the sideways travel at min(dtf, 0.12) s and lowers the wire by min(4.9 t^2, H + Lb - 0.004), about the whole cell height, so the wire ends up inside the cylinder. physics/homopolar.jl only sets off_t, with no free flight and no contact with the board.
findings.suggestion: When the dimple lets go, hand the wire to a free rigid body (its velocity w*e plus its spin) that falls and comes to rest on the board beside the cell, visibly. Move the camera closer so each wire fills the frame.
findings.what: The wire that 'flies off' does not fly off. It slides a few millimetres, then drops straight down into the magnet and battery and disappears into the body. It is a scripted transform, not simulated.
findings.where: a-wire-that-spins-by-itself, storyboard frames 2-5 (left cell) and the 25/50/75% frames; movies/homopolar.jl:68-76

findings.evidence: Every frame is open sea, sky and cloud reflections with one 27 cm white sliver. The rail and post are built at x0 - 0.2, but the camera trails the dart from 1.7 m away looking out to sea, and the rail never enters the frame. At each cut the previous dart jumps to z = -60 m. There is no water contact and no label for down 4, up 4 or up 20.
findings.suggestion: Open each shot on the dart sitting on the rail and leaving it, follow it until it touches the water (with a ripple or a float), and mark each shot (a card, or the bend visible in a close-up). Or show all three paths at once, for example with fading trails, so the dive, glide and rear-up can be compared.
findings.what: Each dart appears out of nothing and ends in nothing. The caption's 'same rail' is never in the picture, no hand or launch is seen, and no landing or splash is seen. The cuts between darts are unmarked, so a viewer cannot tell which fold is which.
findings.where: three-paper-darts, storyboard frames 1, 6 and 11 (cuts), every frame; movies/glider.jl:59-63, 79-82

findings.evidence: physics/glider.jl and physics/homopolar.jl are only included from movies/*.jl. No plugin registers a dart or motor system. homopolar.jl's own header notes 'swap it in ... when this goes live'.
findings.suggestion: Put the dart (fold and throw from the rail) and the motor bench into the live game as plugins, and film the magnet stone gathering spikes and the compass swinging. That is new playable physics that is currently unshown.
findings.what: What the session actually built into the game, a magnet stone that pulls iron spikes and a floating compass that swings to it, is not posted. The posted work is offline movie physics that a player cannot touch.

fun_why: The three darts are tiny white slivers over empty sea with nothing to show where they start or land, and the motors are a few thin orange lines at 960 px, one barely turning, so there is little to watch twice.
real_change: In the game: only the two plugins this session changed, the magnet stone (14 iron spikes magnetised by a ferrite block's surface-charge field, pulled by (m.grad)B, turned by m x B, held by Coulomb friction, sticking on contact) and the compass bowl (a needle on a floating pad turned by m x B from the island's field plus the stone's, damped by a Stokes layer). Neither appears in either post. Both posted films come from offline modules run only inside a movie script. physics/glider.jl is a real vortex lattice plus rigid-body solve over the folded panels (linear lift, no stall, induced velocity turned off). movies/glider.jl only places the result as a transform and hides the two darts not in the shot 60 m under the island. physics/homopolar.jl is a 1-DOF spin-up: Biot-Savart torque on the wire path, friction, drag and a fitted 'c_bounce' damping. The fly-off is just a flag (w > w_off). What the film shows after it (a short slide, then a drop of up to the cell's height) is hand-written in movies/homopolar.jl:68-76. The 'too tight' wire is the same heart with squeeze typed in as 0.6 mm.
real_why: The glider's vortex lattice over arbitrary folded panels holds up and is general (about 6). The motor is a one-axis rig with a fitted damping constant, a typed-in squeeze and a scripted fly-off (at most 5), and both are offline and not part of the playable game.
summary: Both films rest on new physics (a vortex-lattice paper dart in 6 degrees of freedom, a Biot-Savart homopolar motor), but neither shows what its caption says. The dart's launch rail and its landings are never on screen, so each dart appears out of nothing over open sea. The wire that 'flies off' sinks straight down into its battery in a scripted drop and does not fly.
surprise_why: A paper dart flying from its own folds and a wire motor computed from its real current path are physics the island never had, but both posts follow the 'three variants side by side' recipe of the logs and tops posts, and neither lives in the game.
